newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close soft on rates rise, strikes.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close soft on rates rise, strikes.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed soft in light trade for the third day running as interest rates rose and university professors joined striking doctors in protest over wage increases, traders said.
The bolsa's leading index slipped 1.4 percent to close at 6,388.43 points as 14.6 million shares traded, worth 2.9 billion bolivars ($6 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
Yield on six month TEM bills, used as a benchmark for wider interest rates, rose 105 basis points to 17.54 percent in the Central Bank's regular Wednesday auction.
Growing labor strife as government ministers stood firm against teachers' and doctors' wage demands further drove investors away from shares.
"Who is going to invest in the bolsa with so much public sector undertainty?" said one broker. "It's confusing for foreigners, and nervous-making for locals."
Among traded issues, 24 fell, 11 rose and five closed flat. Leading stock Electricidad de Caracas lost 11.00 bolivars to end at 478.95.
Among other widely-held shares, Sivensa slipped 5.10 bolivars to end at 320.00 bolivars, while national telephone company CANTV dropped 30.50 bolivars to close at 1935.00.
